payload.name: Preference-subject attribution from first-person cues
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when a message expresses a preference or opinion using first-person forms (I, my, love, enjoy) and another participant is mentioned in the session; ensure the memory subject is the speaker, not that other participant.
content: During extraction, if a message uses first-person evaluative forms ('I', 'my', 'I love', 'I enjoy') about a person, team, or thing, set the memory subject to the message's speaker. Do not reassign the subject to another participant only because that person was discussed earlier in the session or appears in the same commit window.

Before ADDing a preference/opinion memory, verify the subject field: if the message states the speaker's own view, the subject must be the speaker. Use a non-speaker subject only when the message explicitly describes that person's preference (e.g., 'Tim loves ...').

If a short reply (e.g., starting with 'Thanks!') continues the speaker's own evaluation, still attribute the memory to the speaker; do not let the addressee or a previously mentioned name override the speaker.

solves: Extraction candidates can misattribute a first-person preference (e.g., 'I love his skills and leadership') to another participant mentioned elsewhere in the same session, creating a memory with the wrong subject. This skill applies when a message contains first-person evaluative cues about a person/team while another entity appears in the conversation context; it requires the memory subject to be the speaker. It does not apply when the message explicitly states a third party's preference.
